newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products steady ahead of Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products steady ahead of Christmas.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady on Tuesday in dull Christmas-eve market, traders said.

Gas oil remained firm with buying from China and Hong Kong where an 80,000-tonne MidEast cargo was shipped for January arrival. Part of this cargo was sold at a premium of $1.30 to Singapore quotes c+f Hong Kong. Talk of a second arbitrage cargo done to China at around $1.00 premium was not confirmed. Fixed price Chinese buying seen at $253/$255 per tonne c+f southern China. Physical gas oil was offered lower from Monday with a Jan 10-14 cargo seen at $32.25 facing a bid at that level. Another offer for Jan 14-18 was seen at $30.30 a barrel.

Jet is strong due to large purchases from North Asia and Indonesia. Traders say North Asia has covered most of its January requirements paying up to $2.50 a barrel over Singapore spot quotes for cargoes to Japan and $2.40 premium for cargoes to South Korea. The premium is about 50 cent more than when the first January cargoes were purchased.
Traders said that Indonesia has also entered the market to buy Janaury jet fuel paying between 15-20 cents premium on a free-on-board Singapore basis for several cargoes.
As a result jet fuel swaps have risen with January regrade traded at $1.60 on Monday, up about 20 cents from Friday.

Fuel oil prices were propped up by low Singapore stocks with cargoes absorbed by China and bunker market ahead of Christmas. Traders said the tight supply was reflected by a major coming out to bid for 180-cst at $127 a tonne, up $3 from Monday, for Jan 10-14 lifting fob. By market close, bids/offers fell to $122/$124. A major lowered its offer of a prompt mixed/cracked LSWR cargo lifting early January from $22 a barrel to $21.50. A major confirmed its usual award of 1.1 million barrels from Indonesia in January but total allotment has yet to be made. Naphtha was steady with little change in paper. January swaps were talked at $23.80/$24.10.--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
